_comment: Eastern Cape Department of Education Grade 10 Geography P1 (The Atmosphere, Geomorphology, Population and Water Resources), November 2019 provincial common examination.
Questions and marking-guideline answers extracted from the text layer of the official PDFs
(paper1.pdf, paper1_memo.pdf) and read against the rendered pages. Figures, maps,
graphs and photographs are described in [FIGURE: ...] brackets inside 'context'. memo_answer is
from the official marking guideline (English); mark allocations such as (2) are kept, one
accepted point per line. Column A/B items use the Grade 12 '[Y ... / Z ...]' style.
FORMAT: Section A The Atmosphere and Geomorphology (Questions 1 and 2) and Section B Population and
Water Resources (Questions 3 and 4), 75 marks each. Candidates answer any THREE of the four
questions, so the paper is out of 225; all four questions are transcribed and the entries sum to 300.
All figures are printed in a separate annexure, tracked as paper1_annexure.pdf. This marking
guideline lists accepted points without mark markers; each accepted point is on its own line and
the '(Any n x m)' instruction is kept. Sub-parts (a)/(b)/(c) are kept in one entry.
OFFICIAL MEMO ERRORS (see memo_note): 1.4.1 swaps the mesosphere and thermosphere (FIGURE 1.4 puts
the mesosphere at C, about 50-85 km, and the thermosphere at D, above 85 km); 4.4.2 swaps the push
and pull labels (FIGURE 4.4 lists health care, education, money, better services, food, jobs and
city life as PULL factors and no money, boredom, poor schools, no jobs, poverty, war and climatic

questions.context: 1.6 Carefully read the case study in FIGURE 1.6 about volcanic eruption in Mount Sinabung, Indonesia. [FIGURE 1.6: VOLCANIC ERUPTION. Photograph of a man holding a child and watching a large column of ash rise from a volcano.] Mount Sinabung: Volcano eruption warnings after huge column of ash prompts panic in Indonesia. A huge column of ash was blasted almost five miles into the sky above the Indonesian island of Sumatra after an active volcano erupted. Indonesian officials warned that further volcanic activity was possible although the volcano's alert level remained unchanged. Residents have been told to stay indoors and to wear face masks, if venturing outside, to protect themselves from volcanic ashfall. Sinabung was inactive for around 400 years before it erupted in 2010, killing two people. Since then it has become one of this South East Asia's most active volcanoes, bringing both negative and positive effects to the nation. More than a dozen people were killed and thousands were forced to flee when it erupted in 2014. Indonesia is particularly prone to seismic activity due to its location on the 'Ring of Fire', an arc of volcanoes and fault lines encircling the Pacific Basin. [Source: https://www.independent.co.uk/news/world/asia/mount-sinabung-volcano-eruption]

questions.context: 2.5 Read the case study in FIGURE 2.5 and answer the questions that follow. [FIGURE 2.5: EARTHQUAKE IN NEPAL. Photograph of collapsed buildings and toppled power poles in a street, captioned NEPAL EARTHQUAKE.] An earthquake, which measured 7,8 on the Richter scale, struck Nepal on April 25, 2015, toppling multi-story buildings in Kathmandu and creating landslides and avalanches in the Himalaya Mountains. It was the deadliest earthquake in the region in 81 years because nearly 9 000 people died and more than 22 000 suffered injuries. Humanitarian organisations responded quickly to the disaster with search and rescue teams and immediate aid deliveries. Work is still underway to rebuild schools, health clinics, houses, livelihoods, and to help families and communities gain more resilience to environmental shocks. questions.context: 3.3 Refer to the case study in FIGURE 3.3 about HIV/Aids and answer the questions that follow. [FIGURE 3.3: KHOMANANI 'CARING TOGETHER' ON HIV/AIDS.] The campaign loveLife has run since 1999 and uses a wide range of media directed mainly towards teens. Aids is one of the main contributors to South Africa's infant mortality rate. In 2016, deaths due to HIV/Aids were estimated to be about 150 376 and 3,7 million people were taking ARV treatment for HIV. By 2018, more than 4,5 million people were taking ARVs. There are several large-scale communication campaigns related to raising awareness of HIV and Aids, as well as broader health-related issues. Khomanani, meaning 'caring together', ran since 2001 and was the government Health Department's premier Aids-awareness campaign. Soul City and Soul Buddyz are two multi-media campaigns - targeted at adults and children, respectively - that have a combined annual budget of R100 million, and utilise broadcast, print and outdoor media to promote good sexual health and well-being. [Source: www.southafrica-pig.blogspot.com]

questions.context: 3.6 Read the case study in FIGURE 3.6 and answer the questions that follow. [FIGURE 3.6: FLOODS IN KWAZULU-NATAL.] At least 51 confirmed dead in KZN floods - reports. At least 51 people have been confirmed dead following flooding in KwaZulu-Natal which was triggered by heavy rains, EWN has reported. KwaZulu-Natal Cooperative Governance MEC Nomusa Dube-Ncube reportedly said that more bodies had been discovered under the rubble as rescue operations continued throughout Tuesday night. Five more people remain unaccounted for, she said. 'Dozens of cases of collapsed walls and flooded homes have been reported, with 235 Durban homes already assessed as damaged. Roads have been flooded too, disrupting traffic. Motorists and pedestrians are urged to exercise utmost caution on the roads that are already flooded or where there is high risk of flash flooding,' said Dube-Ncube. Authorities had reported 145 displaced persons, some of whom had already found shelter with relatives. Dube-Ncube urged residents and visitors to the province to remain on full alert and to move to higher ground if under threat. [Source: https://www.news24.com/SouthAfrica/News]

questions.context: 4.6 Refer to FIGURE 4.6 and answer the following questions. [FIGURE 4.6: FISHING POPULATION CRUSHED BY 50%. WWF infographic: 'FISH POPULATIONS ESSENTIAL FOR FOOD AND JOBS HAVE CRASHED BY 50% IN THE LAST 4 DECADES', with fishing boats and nets over a shoal of fish on a 1970-2010 time line.] Many people in South Africa depend on fish as a source of food and income. In South Africa the fisheries industry is worth R6 billion and employs over 27 000 people. Overfishing and illegal fishing threatens the livelihoods of people employed in the industry. It also threatens vulnerable ecosystems and marine animals such as seals, coastal birds, and larger fish that depend on fish as a source of food. There's only a limited amount of fish in our oceans, and those resources are becoming depleted. According to the World Wildlife Fund (WWF) more than 30% of the world's fisheries have been overfished and is in need of strict management to restore them. Target fishing of top predators like tuna is changing marine communities. Because of commercial fishing, populations of the Atlantic Bluefin tuna have declined to the point where their survival as a species is threatened. However, we can solve this problem by reforming fisheries management. [Source: https://www.westerncape.gov.za/general-publication/overfishing]
